description: Fleet overview for mitmania: traffic, fail-closed policy outcomes, upstream health, storage, rules, certificates, TLS, and broker outcalls. Successful mitm:false traffic is reported as splice (mitm:false); empty-connection is shown as neutral listener churn.

panels.description: Open client connections across the selected fleet.
panels.title: Active connections

panels.description: Successful raw encrypted splices per second. mitm:false does not expose method, path, headers, or body.
panels.title: Encrypted splices

panels.description: Requests denied by security gates: no matching connection rule, egress/self-listener refusal, or proxy authentication. Deliberate rule blocks are charted below but excluded here.
panels.title: Fail-closed denials

panels.description: Share of upstream connection attempts whose final result is not ok.
panels.title: Upstream dial errors

panels.description: 95th percentile TCP+TLS upstream dial time for successful dials.
panels.title: Upstream dial p95

panels.description: Selected mitmania service instances visible to Prometheus.
panels.title: Nodes reporting

panels.description: Request/tunnel rate by final outcome. Splice is successful mitm:false traffic; empty-connection is neutral listener churn. Policy and egress decisions remain distinct.
panels.title: Final outcomes

panels.description: Open connections separated by node, listener, and transport.
panels.title: Connection concurrency

panels.description: New client connections accepted per second, separated by listener and transport.
panels.title: Accepted connection rate

panels.description: Request handler bookkeeping latency by protocol. For mitm:false splices this measures setup/handling, not tunnel lifetime or origin latency.
panels.title: Handler duration percentiles

panels.description: Current time-range request composition. Empty connections and successful encrypted splices are intentionally distinct.
panels.title: Outcome composition

panels.description: Upstream connection attempts by final result. Timeout, refused, DNS, and TLS failures describe the origin or egress path.
panels.title: Upstream dial results

panels.description: Successful upstream TCP+TLS dial latency. Failed-result latency is excluded so timeouts do not distort normal-origin performance.
panels.title: Successful dial latency

panels.description: Storage operation throughput by backend, operation, and result. POSIX stat errors can be normal cache-probe misses; interpret them alongside outcome and latency rather than as an outage by themselves.
panels.title: Storage operations

panels.description: 95th percentile Storage call latency by backend and operation, separated by result.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, backend, op, result) (rate(mitmania_storage_op_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Storage latency p95

panels.description: Upstream time-to-first-byte when message-phase HTTP telemetry is available. A blank panel is expected for a pure mitm:false deployment.
panels.title: Upstream TTFB

panels.description: Rule file compiles by result. Any error means a node could not compile a Storage update and retains the prior in-memory rules.
panels.title: Rule compile events

panels.description: Rule parse and compile latency by result.
panels.title: Rule compile latency p95

panels.description: Clients with an effective compiled rule set in memory. This metric appears after per-client rule sets are loaded.
panels.title: Active client rule sets
MITM, certificates & broker outcalls · panels appear when these paths are used

panels.description: TLS handshake p95 by client/upstream leg and result. A pure mitm:false deployment is expected to have no series here.
panels.title: TLS handshake latency p95

panels.description: Certificate cache lookup rate. A healthy warm fleet is dominated by hotmap and storage hits; sustained misses plus leaf mints indicate churn or self-heal.
panels.title: Certificate cache

panels.description: Broker decision rate by action and result. result=fail denies traffic under the default fail-closed behavior.
panels.title: Outcall decisions

panels.description: Current process-wide broker concurrency relative to the configured --outcall-max-inflight value. At the limit, new outcalls fail closed.
panels.title: Outcall saturation

panels.description: Streaming payload throughput by direction. This metric appears when message bodies or tunnel streams report transferred bytes.
panels.title: Stream throughput

panels.description: Upstream connections replaced mid-session, separated by reason.
panels.title: Upstream reconnects

title: mitmania · Security Proxy Operations
